title: AGI, ASI, RSI and the Singularity: What Each Claim Actually Means
summary: A disciplined separation of four ideas that are often collapsed together: broadly general AI capability, superhuman intelligence, recursive self-improvement, and a hypothesized discontinuity in technological change.
eli5: AGI asks how general an AI is, ASI asks whether it greatly exceeds humans, RSI asks whether an AI can improve the process that improves itself, and the singularity is a prediction about what society and technological progress might look like if capability growth becomes extremely fast or hard to forecast.

sections.heading: Four different claims
columns: What it does not automatically imply
rows: AGI
Broad/general competence across a large range of cognitive tasks
Consciousness, embodiment, full autonomy or superhuman performance at everything
ASI
Intelligence/capability far beyond human performance across important domains
A specific architecture, values, goals or inevitability
RSI
An improvement process feeds improvements back into its own future improvement capability
Runaway improvement, unlimited progress or model-weight self-editing
Technological singularity
A hypothesized future transition after which technological change becomes unusually rapid or difficult to predict from today's perspective
A scientifically established date or a necessary consequence of AGI

sections.heading: AGI has no single universally accepted finish line
sections.body: Definitions differ over breadth, performance, autonomy, embodiment and economic usefulness. One useful approach is to separate performance depth from task generality and treat autonomy as a deployment dimension rather than silently baking every property into one label. This makes arguments about whether 'AGI is here' easier to inspect: people may be using different thresholds.

sections.heading: ASI is a relative capability concept
sections.body: Artificial superintelligence normally refers to systems whose relevant cognitive capabilities substantially exceed human performance. The term does not settle how such a system would be built, whether it would be one model or a larger system, whether it would be conscious, or what goals it would pursue. Those are additional claims.

sections.heading: Self-improvement has levels
rows: Self-refinement
Generate an answer, critique it, revise it
The model improves an output, not necessarily itself
Harness adaptation
An AI proposes better prompts, tools, routing or tests
The surrounding system changes; acceptance can remain externally verified
Training-loop improvement
AI helps create data, rewards, architectures or training code
The system contributes to future model capability but humans/infrastructure may still gate it
Open-ended RSI
Successive improvements substantially improve the ability to generate the next improvements
The strongest recursive claim; evidence for sustained runaway dynamics remains uncertain

sections.heading: RSI is not a synonym for 'AI edits its own code'
sections.body: A system can modify code without making itself more capable, and it can contribute to capability improvement without directly rewriting its own weights. The key question is whether the improvement process improves the future improvement process in a sustained, validated loop.

sections.heading: Why the singularity is epistemically different
sections.body: The singularity is a forecast or scenario family, not an observed technical mechanism. Arguments usually combine assumptions about capability progress, automation of research, economic feedback, deployment speed and limits such as compute, data, verification, institutions or physical bottlenecks. Changing any of those assumptions can change the conclusion.

sections.heading: How to evaluate a dramatic claim
sections.question: Someone says: 'Once we get AGI, RSI starts immediately and ASI follows in months.'
sections.diagnosis: The statement compresses at least three uncertain transitions into one sentence: reaching a chosen AGI threshold, closing a reliable self-improvement loop, and sustaining a rate of improvement sufficient to reach the chosen ASI threshold quickly.
sections.resolution: Ask for each transition separately: definition, mechanism, bottlenecks, verification signal, resource assumptions and empirical evidence. Treat timelines as forecasts rather than consequences of the acronyms themselves.

sections.heading: Check yourself
sections.question: Could an AGI exist without RSI?
sections.answer: Yes. General capability and recursive self-improvement are separate properties. A broadly capable system might not have access to or competence at improving its own development process, or such improvements might remain externally gated.
